questions.question:
Read the given statements and conclusions carefully. Assuming that the information given in the statements is true, even if it appears to be at variance with commonly known facts, decide which of the given conclusions logically follow(s) from the statements.

**Statements:**

Some daisies are lilies.

All roses are lilies.

Some tulips are daisies.

**Conclusions:**

(I) Some lilies are tulips.

(II) Some roses are daisies.
questions.solution:
The least possible Venn diagram for the given statements is as shown below :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c1f270006fb1b6618f856d0ed596df60170d692fe9177c20b5f1daa726452e74.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some lilies are tulips → Does not follow (As some daisies are lilies and some tulips are daisies. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

II. Some roses are daisies → Does not follow (As some daisies are lilies and all roses are lilies. So, it is possible but not definitely true)

∴ Here, Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Neither conclusion (I) nor (II) follows**".

questions.question: In the middle of which century did the Arab traveler Sulaiman visit India?

• He was an Arab traveler and merchant who wrote about his travels in a book called **"Kitab al-Masalik wa al-Mamalik"** (Book of Roads and Kingdoms).
 
• Sulaiman's account of his journey provides valuable information about the **political, social, and economic** conditions of India during that time.

• The **11th century** saw the reign of **King Rajendra Chola**, who expanded the Chola Empire through conquest and trade.
 
• The **6th century **was a time of political and social upheaval in India, with the **decline of the Gupta Empire** and the emergence of regional kingdoms.

questions.question: Net domestic product is calculated as _________.

options.text: GDP - Net income earned from abroad

The correct answer is __**GDP - Depreciation.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__ Key Points__**

__
 
• **Net domestic product** (NDP) is the **total value of goods and services** produced within a country's borders, **minus the depreciation **of capital goods.
 
• **Depreciation** is the **decrease in value of an asset **over time due to wear and tear, obsolescence, or other factors.
 
• **GDP - Depreciation** is the correct answer because it** subtracts** the amount of capital goods that have been consumed or used up in the production process from the gross domestic product (GDP).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **GNP - Depreciation **is incorrect because it** subtracts** the amount of capital goods used up in the production process from the** gross national product (GNP)**, which measures the total value of goods and services produced by a** country's residents,** regardless of their location.
 
• **Gross domestic product **(GDP) is the total value of goods and services produced within a **country's borders, **regardless of the nationality of the producers.
 
• **Gross national product** (GNP) is the** total value of goods and services** produced by a country's residents, regardless of their location.
 
• **Net income earned from abroad** is the **difference** between the income earned by a country's residents from **abroad **(such as from foreign investments or employment) and the income earned by **foreigners** within the country.
 
• **Depreciation** is an important factor to consider in **calculating NDP** because it reflects the **decrease **in the value of capital goods over time and the need for reinvestment in new capital goods to maintain or increase production levels.
